class.name: IcyAudioDecoder
class.brief_description: Generic audio decoder class providing a common interface for audio stream decoders with buffering support.
class.description:
[IcyAudioDecoder] is the base class for audio stream decoders and owns the whole streaming pipeline: incoming encoded data is held in a fixed 512 KiB jitter buffer (when it overflows the oldest bytes are dropped and [signal buffer_overrun] is emitted), decoded in fixed-size batches from [method process_audio] and pushed into an [AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback]. It also provides the buffering mechanism, including configurable buffer thresholds, buffering state tracking, and notifications when buffering starts or finishes. Decoding does not start until roughly one second of encoded data has been buffered (see [method set_bitrate_hint]); the same amount is buffered again whenever the codec runs out of data.
[b]Note:[/b] Derived classes only implement the codec itself (probe, decode a batch, reset); everything else is shared.

signal.name: buffering_started
signal.description: Emitted when the buffered audio data has been depleted and the decoder enters the buffering state. Emitted synchronously from [method process_audio].

signal.name: buffering_finished
signal.description: Emitted when the buffered audio data reaches the configured target threshold and buffering completes. Emitted synchronously from [method process_audio].

signal.name: stream_info_ready
signal.description: Emitted from inside [method process_audio] (synchronously, on the main thread) once the decoder has read enough of the stream to determine its sample rate and channel count. This happens before a playback is required, so a handler can set the generator's [code]mix_rate[/code] from [method get_stream_sample_rate], start the player and then call [method set_playback] with the freshly created playback. No audio is decoded until a playback has been set.

signal.name: buffer_overrun
signal.description: Emitted when incoming encoded data arrives faster than it is consumed and the internal jitter buffer (512 KiB) overflows. The oldest [param dropped_bytes] bytes are discarded so playback stays near the live edge. Usually means [method process_audio] is not being called regularly. The signal is emitted deferred because the overflow is detected on the download thread.

method.name: set_playback
method.description: Sets the [AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback] instance used by the decoder for buffer management. This playback object is used to determine the current buffering state and available audio frames. The maximum buffer capacity is observed directly from the playback's ring buffer rather than computed, so no generator or capacity value needs to be supplied. Call this again with a freshly instantiated playback whenever the generator's [code]mix_rate[/code] or [code]buffer_length[/code] changes.

method.name: set_buffer_thresholds
method.description: Configures the buffering threshold used by the decoder. [code]target_frames[/code] specifies the number of buffered frames required before buffering is considered complete.

method.name: process_audio
method.description: Processes decoder-specific audio handling and moves raw audio frame data into the [AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback]'s ring buffer. Call it regularly (e.g. from a [Timer] or [method Node._process]); the decoder sizes its work to the space available in the playback. [b]Note:[/b] Must be called from the main thread. All signals raised from it ([signal buffering_started], [signal buffering_finished] and [signal stream_info_ready]) are emitted directly, not deferred, so their handlers run before this method returns.

method.name: reset
method.description: Discards all buffered encoded data and the codec state, so the decoder probes the stream again from scratch. Use it to reuse one decoder instance across reconnects instead of creating a new one. Must be called from the main thread.

method.name: set_bitrate_hint
method.description: Sets the amount of encoded data (in bytes) that must be buffered before decoding starts, and before it resumes after the codec has run out of data, to roughly one second of audio at [param kbps]. The threshold is [code]max((kbps * 1000) / 8, floor)[/code], where [code]floor[/code] is the minimum amount the codec needs to probe the stream (16384 bytes for MP3, so streams below 128 kbps all use the floor, which for them is more than one second of audio). If this method is not called, the floor is used. Non-positive values are ignored.

method.name: get_stream_sample_rate
method.description: Returns the sample rate of the incoming stream, or [code]0[/code] until [signal stream_info_ready] has been emitted.

method.name: get_stream_channels
method.description: Returns the channel count of the incoming stream, or [code]0[/code] until [signal stream_info_ready] has been emitted.

method.name: get_buffering_progress
method.description: Returns the current buffering progress as a value between [code]0.0[/code] and [code]1.0[/code].

method.name: is_buffering
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the decoder is currently buffering audio data, otherwise returns [code]false[/code].

method.name: get_current_target_frames
method.description: Returns the current target number of buffered frames required before playback can resume after buffering.

method.name: get_current_max_capacity_frames
method.description: Returns the observed maximum capacity of the playback ring buffer, expressed in audio frames. Intended for debugging.

method.name: create_for_mime_type
method.description: Creates and returns a new decoder instance for [code]mime_type[/code] (e.g. [code]"audio/mpeg"[/code]) using the decoder that was registered for it, or [code]null[/code] if no decoder is registered for that MIME type. Decoders register themselves at extension init time; use this instead of hand-rolling a content-type [code]match[/code], so a future decoder module can add support for its own MIME type without callers needing to change.
